```
without argument.

[WHERE A PERMIT IS REQUIRED: The completed application form is
enclosed, together with the fee of [AMOUNT] [/ and I would be grateful
if you would tell me the fee and how it should be paid]. If anything
further is required to complete the application, please tell me and I
will provide it the same week.]

[WHERE THE POLICE DEPARTMENT IS THE ADDRESSEE OR IS COPIED: Our
stewards will direct our own participants and will not direct traffic
or members of the public. If your department considers a traffic post
necessary at [LOCATION], I would be grateful to know the cost of
officers on private duty and how that is arranged, and the Kingdom
will meet it.]

I would welcome a short conversation with whoever will handle this,
and I am content to change the [route / time / arrangements] to suit
your operational preferences. It is easier to change them now than on
the day.

If I have not heard from your office by [DATE, AT LEAST TWO WEEKS
BEFORE THE EVENT], I will telephone. If this application belongs with
another office, please tell me which and I will write to them
directly.

Thank you for your time.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Completed [FORM NAME]
             2. Route map / site plan
             3. Certificate of insurance
             4. [Steward plan, where the numbers warrant one]

cc:          [CHIEF OF POLICE / DISTRICT COMMANDER]
             [FIRE MARSHAL, WHERE OCCUPANCY OR OPEN FLAME IS
             INVOLVED]
             [PUBLIC WORKS, WHERE STREET FURNITURE OR CLEANING IS
             INVOLVED]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Send it early. The single most common cause of a refused event is an application
that arrived inside the ordinance's notice period, and no First Amendment
argument repairs a late filing that a secular applicant would also have lost.
Find the required period in the ordinance before choosing the date of the event,
not after.

Every condition imposed goes in the file with the reason given, in writing. Where
a condition is imposed on the Kingdom's gathering that is not imposed on
comparable gatherings — a fee, an officer requirement, a restriction on hours,
an insurance limit — do not argue about it on the telephone. Get the condition in
writing, ask courteously for the authority under which it is imposed, and record
what comparable events were required to do. That record is the whole of the
equal-terms case if one is ever needed, and it can only be built at the time.

Confirm every operational agreement by email within a business day, closing with
the sentence that does the work: *if I have misunderstood anything, please tell me
and I will correct my record.*

---

# 8. Request for extra patrol or a security assessment

## When to use this

Use it after a threat, after an incident, before a gathering that has attracted
hostile attention, or where a general climate makes it prudent. It is a request
for help, made to a department that has no obligation to grant it, and it should
read that way.

Be clear-eyed about what is being asked. No statute entitles any private body to
police protection, and the Kingdom should not suggest otherwise. What departments
do have is discretion, a directed-patrol or special-attention mechanism that costs
them almost nothing, crime prevention officers who conduct site assessments as a
matter of routine, and, in most places, a private-duty arrangement under which a
department will assign officers at the requester's expense. All three are
obtainable by a body that asks properly. None is obtainable by a body that
demands.

The letter is also worth sending for a reason unrelated to patrol. A dated
request describing a specific threat creates a record that the department was on
notice, and that record has value both in any later grant application and, if
matters ever go badly, in every account of what was known and when.

## What must accompany it

The incident record numbers for anything already reported. A short schedule of
prior incidents if there are any. A site plan or address list where an assessment
is sought. Nothing rhetorical.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY FIRST-CLASS MAIL

[FULL NAME]
[Chief of Police / Commander, [DISTRICT] / Community Services
 Division]
[NAME] Police Department
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY], Connecticut [ZIP]

Re:  Request for special attention and a security assessment —
     [ADDRESS OF THE PLACE OF WORSHIP]
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [SALUTATION]:

I am [FULL NAME], [OFFICE HELD] of Apex Kingdom, a religious society
and charitable trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT]. I write to ask for
your department's assistance in two specific and modest respects.

1. WHY WE ARE ASKING

   [THE FACTS, BRIEFLY AND WITHOUT ADJECTIVES — e.g., "On [DATE] the
   Kingdom reported criminal mischief at its premises (case number
   [NUMBER]). On [DATE] a further message was received at the
   premises, reported under case number [NUMBER]. The Kingdom holds
   services on [DAY] evenings between [TIME] and [TIME], when
   approximately [NUMBER] people including children are present, and
   the car park is unlit at those hours."]

2. WHAT IS ASKED

   (a) Special attention or directed patrol at [ADDRESS] during
       [SPECIFIC HOURS AND DAYS], for [PERIOD — e.g., "the next
       ninety days"], to whatever extent your patrol commitments
       allow.

   (b) A security assessment of the premises by your crime prevention
       officer, at a time convenient to the department, so that we can
       act on your officers' recommendations about lighting, access,
       sight lines, and camera placement. We will implement what we
       can afford and will tell you what we have done.

   [WHERE AN EVENT IS THE OCCASION: (c) A conversation before our
   gathering on [DATE], described in my letter of [DATE], about
   whether the department wishes any arrangement on the day. If
   officers on private duty are appropriate, please tell me the cost
   and how it is arranged; the Kingdom will meet it.]

   The Kingdom is not asking for anything to be given priority over
   your department's other commitments, and I understand that patrol
   resources are allocated on operational judgments that are yours to
   make.

3. WHAT WE HAVE DONE OURSELVES

   [BRIEFLY — e.g., "We have installed two cameras covering the north
   and east doors, retaining footage for [NUMBER] days; we lock the
   [LOCATION] gate outside service hours; and we have asked members
   to report anything unusual to me rather than approach anyone."]

   Our volunteers steward our own gatherings and do not patrol,
   detain, or approach anyone. Anything requiring a response beyond
   locking a door is reported to your department by telephone.

Our liaison for your department is [NAME], [TELEPHONE], [EMAIL],
available [HOURS], and [NAME] holds keys and can attend the premises
at any hour if your officers need access.

I will telephone the Community Services Division on [DATE] to ask
about the assessment if I have not heard before then.

Thank you for considering this, and for the work your officers do in
[NEIGHBOURHOOD].

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Schedule of reported incidents with case numbers
             2. Site plan showing entrances, lighting, and camera
                positions

cc:          [DISTRICT COMMANDER, WHERE THE LETTER GOES TO THE CHIEF]
             [LIAISON OFFICER]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Email and first-class mail. Never certified — certified mail on a request for
help reads as the opening of a file against the recipient, which is exactly the
wrong signal.

Record what is granted and what is not. Where an assessment is done, act on the
recommendations within the Kingdom's means and write back saying what was done;
that letter costs nothing and is the reason the department returns the next call.

Two things follow from a documented threat picture and both are worth pursuing.
The federal Nonprofit Security Grant Program funds physical security improvements
for at-risk nonprofit organisations, including houses of worship, and is
administered through the state administrative agency rather than applied for
directly to Washington — confirm the current cycle, eligibility conditions, and
the state contact before building anything around it. And the Kingdom's insurer
will often reduce a premium for the same measures. Both applications are far
stronger with a police assessment and dated case numbers behind them, which is
another reason to send this letter before it is urgent.

---

# 9. Request to a municipality for religious land-use accommodation

## When to use this

Use it where a municipal land-use decision, condition, requirement, or
interpretation prevents or seriously impedes the Kingdom's religious use of
property: a permit denied or stalled, a use classification that excludes
worship from a zone where comparable secular assembly is allowed, a parking or
occupancy condition that makes the use impossible, an enforcement action against
an existing use.

**This letter is written to be read by a town attorney, and everything about it
follows from that.** The planner will forward it; the attorney will decide the
response. That reader is not moved by indignation, is not frightened by a threat,
and has advised around RLUIPA before. What that reader is moved by is a letter
that is temperate, factually specific, obviously prepared, and explicit that the
sender would rather solve this than sue — because that is the letter that lets
the attorney recommend a solution without appearing to have been pushed into one.

Read `04-GOVERNMENT-RELATIONS-PROTOCOL` § 6 before drafting. It says not to name
RLUIPA in the first letter, and that remains right: invoking the statute at the
staff stage converts a solvable problem into a litigation posture, and the town
stops talking and starts documenting. **This is not the first letter.** This is
the letter sent after the ordinary application has been made properly, the
decision or the impasse has come, and the ordinary channels are exhausted. If
that is not where the matter stands, use `government-correspondence` instead and
come back to this later.

The statute, accurately. RLUIPA, 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc, has two provisions that
matter here. Section 2000cc(a) prohibits a land use regulation that imposes a
substantial burden on religious exercise unless the government shows a compelling
governmental interest pursued by the least restrictive means — but only where a
jurisdictional trigger in § 2000cc(a)(2) is met, of which the one that operates
in practice is that the government makes individualised assessments of proposed
uses, as a zoning or special permit authority does. Section 2000cc(b)(1)
separately bars treating a religious assembly or institution on less than equal
terms with a non-religious assembly or institution, and needs no such trigger.
"Religious exercise" is defined at 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc-5, and includes the use of
real property for religious exercise; a private cause of action and relief are
provided at 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc-2.

Two limits to keep in front of you. RLUIPA is not a permit and excuses nobody
from applying; building or occupying without approval forfeits the posture the
statute depends on. And a Connecticut land-use appeal must be commenced within
fifteen days of publication of notice of the decision, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 8-8(b),
a period that is jurisdictional. **A courteous accommodation dialogue will run
that clock out if nobody is watching it.** Compute the appeal date the day the
decision is published, before this letter is drafted, and treat it as immovable.

Be certain first which clock is running, because there are two and this template
is addressed to both situations. Section 8-8 governs an appeal from the decision
of a board — a zoning commission, a planning commission, a zoning board of
appeals. An order of a zoning enforcement officer, which is what a notice of
violation or a cease-and-desist order usually is, is not a decision of a board.
It is appealed first to the zoning board of appeals under Conn. Gen. Stat.
§§ 8-6 and 8-7, within the period that board's own rules prescribe, and § 8-8
governs only the appeal from what the board then decides. Confirm the board's
rule and the period it sets before computing anything, and confirm both against
the current General Statutes. Reading the fifteen-day period onto a zoning
enforcement officer's notice is how an appeal is brought in the wrong forum while
the right one closes, and that is not a mistake anyone can repair afterwards.
The § 8-8 appeal to the Superior Court — not the appeal to the board — is
commenced by service of process rather than by filing, and service is made by a
state marshal, so counsel and a marshal have to be engaged with days in hand and
not on the fifteenth.

This letter should also not go out until counsel has read it. It names a federal
statute, which means the first question the town attorney asks is whether the
Kingdom is represented, and the answer changes the reply that gets drafted. A
RLUIPA paragraph over the signature of a lay principal with no lawyer behind it
is read as posturing; the same paragraph with counsel copied is read as a
position the town will have to answer.

## What must accompany it

The comparison, which is the entire strength of the letter: what the ordinance
permits by right or by special permit in the same zone for non-religious
assembly, and what the town has actually required of those applicants. That
material comes from the ordinance and from records requests made months earlier
in the ordinary course — which is why `connecticut-foia-request` is sent early
rather than at this stage.

Also: the application and its decision, the stated reasons, the site plan, and a
short factual statement of the burden with numbers in it.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY CERTIFIED MAIL, RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED

[FULL NAME]
[Director of Planning and Zoning / Zoning Enforcement Officer /
 Chairman, [BOARD]]
[CITY OR TOWN] of [NAME]
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY], Connecticut [ZIP]

Re:  [ADDRESS OF THE PROPERTY] — [Application No. [NUMBER] /
     Notice of Violation No. [NUMBER]]
     Request for accommodation of religious use
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [SALUTATION]:

I write on behalf of Apex Kingdom, a religious society and charitable
trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT], concerning [THE PROPERTY] and the
[decision of [DATE] / condition imposed on [DATE] / position taken by
your office on [DATE]]. The Kingdom would like to resolve this with
the [CITY] rather than take it anywhere else, and this letter is an
attempt to do that.

1. THE RELIGIOUS USE

   The Kingdom is a religious society. Its use of [THE PROPERTY] is
   [DESCRIBE CONCRETELY — e.g., "assembly for worship on [DAYS] at
   [TIMES], religious instruction for [NUMBER] children on [DAY],
   and the preparation and distribution of meals as an exercise of
   its religious obligation to the poor"]. [WHERE THE RELIGIOUS
   CHARACTER OF A PARTICULAR REQUIREMENT MATTERS, SAY WHY IN ONE
   SENTENCE, WITHOUT ARGUING THEOLOGY.]

   The religious character of the use was stated in the application
   of [DATE] and has been on the record from the outset.

2. WHAT THE CITY HAS DECIDED, AND WHAT IT MEANS IN PRACTICE

   [THE DECISION OR REQUIREMENT, QUOTED OR CITED EXACTLY, WITH ITS
   DATE AND THE REASONS THE CITY GAVE.]

   The practical effect is [SPECIFIC, WITH NUMBERS — e.g., "that the
   Kingdom cannot assemble for worship at the property at all";
   "that the Kingdom must provide [NUMBER] parking spaces on a site
   that can physically accommodate [NUMBER], which cannot be done";
   "that a use the Kingdom has carried on at this address since
   [YEAR] must cease within [NUMBER] days"]. The Kingdom has looked
   for alternatives: [WHAT WAS TRIED AND WHY IT DID NOT WORK — e.g.,
   "three other properties in the [ZONE] district were viewed
   between [DATE] and [DATE]; two were beyond the Kingdom's means at
   [AMOUNT] per month and the third is subject to the same
   requirement"].

3. HOW COMPARABLE USES ARE TREATED

   [THIS IS THE PARAGRAPH THAT DOES THE WORK. BE EXACT AND
   VERIFIABLE. e.g., "Section [NUMBER] of the [CITY] Zoning
   Regulations permits [clubs and lodges / theatres / banquet halls /
   community centres] in the [ZONE] district [by right / by special
   permit]. The [BOARD] approved application No. [NUMBER] for [NAME
   OF SECULAR ASSEMBLY USE] at [ADDRESS] on [DATE], in the same
   district, with [NUMBER] parking spaces and without the condition
   imposed here."] These facts come from the [CITY]'s own records,
   provided in response to my request of [DATE].

4. WHAT IS ASKED

   The Kingdom asks the [CITY] to [THE SPECIFIC, GRANTABLE REMEDY —
   e.g., "treat the proposed use as a permitted assembly use in the
   [ZONE] district on the same terms as the uses identified above";
   "grant the modification of the parking requirement provided for
   at § [NUMBER] of the Regulations"; "withdraw the notice of
   violation of [DATE] and allow the existing use to continue"].

   [OFFER SOMETHING. e.g., "The Kingdom is willing to accept
   conditions limiting assembly to [HOURS], to fund the [NUMBER]
   off-street spaces identified on the enclosed plan, and to enter
   a shared-parking arrangement with [OWNER], who has agreed in
   principle."]

5. THE LEGAL FRAMEWORK, STATED ONCE

   The Kingdom raises this because the Religious Land Use and
   Institutionalized Persons Act, 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc, is engaged on
   these facts. Section 2000cc(a) prohibits the imposition of a land
   use regulation that substantially burdens religious exercise
   unless the government demonstrates a compelling interest pursued
   by the least restrictive means, where — as with the individualised
   assessments made under your special permit procedure — a
   jurisdictional trigger in § 2000cc(a)(2) is met. Section
   2000cc(b)(1) separately requires that a religious assembly not be
   treated on less than equal terms with a non-religious assembly.

   I set that out because it would be discourteous to leave it
   unsaid and then rely on it, not because the Kingdom wishes to
   litigate. It does not. Litigation is slow and expensive for a
   small religious body and for the [CITY] alike, and the outcome
   the Kingdom actually wants is a place to worship in this
   neighbourhood on the same terms as the [CITY]'s other assemblies.
   If the [CITY] and the Kingdom can reach that outcome, nothing in
   this paragraph will be heard from again.

6. WHAT WE PROPOSE NEXT

   I would welcome a meeting with you, with the Office of the City
   Attorney, and with anyone else you think should be present, at
   your offices and at your convenience within the next [NUMBER]
   weeks. I am content to come alone or with counsel, whichever the
   [CITY] would prefer.

   [WHERE AN APPEAL PERIOD IS RUNNING, SAY SO WITHOUT MENACE, AND
   NAME THE RIGHT PROVISION — § 8-8(b) FOR A DECISION OF A BOARD,
   §§ 8-6 AND 8-7 AND THE BOARD'S OWN RULE FOR AN APPEAL FROM A
   ZONING ENFORCEMENT OFFICER: The Kingdom notes that the period for
   an appeal under [PROVISION] expires on [DATE]. It would prefer to
   resolve this by agreement, but it cannot allow that period to
   lapse, and I mention the date so that the timetable is clear to
   both of us rather than a surprise to either.]

If I have not heard from your office by [DATE], I will telephone. If
any factual statement above is wrong, please tell me and I will
correct it; I would rather be corrected now than be relying on a
mistake.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Application No. [NUMBER] and decision of [DATE]
             2. Site plan
             3. Schedule of comparable approvals in the [ZONE]
                district, with application numbers and dates
             4. [Records provided by the [CITY] on [DATE]]

cc:          [NAME], Esq., Office of the City Attorney
             [COUNSEL FOR THE KINGDOM]
             [NOT THE CHAIRMAN OR ANY MEMBER OF A BOARD OR
             COMMISSION THAT HAS THE MATTER BEFORE IT — SEE BELOW]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Certified mail with return receipt and email, with the City Attorney copied by
name from the outset. Copying the attorney is not an escalation here; it is the
courtesy that gets the letter to the person who will decide, and it prevents the
answer that nobody in a position to settle ever saw it.

Do not copy the chairman or any member of a board or commission that has the
application before it. Those bodies act quasi-judicially on an individualised
application, and correspondence reaching a member outside the record is an ex
parte communication — which town counsel then has to deal with, which can taint
the very decision the Kingdom is asking for, and which tells the attorney that
the applicant does not understand the proceeding they are in. Everything meant for
the commission goes into the record through staff or at the hearing, where it can
be relied on afterwards.

Then hold two things simultaneously and do not let either slip. Pursue the
meeting genuinely, prepare a written note of it within a business day, and
confirm anything agreed. And keep the appeal date immovable. The commonest way a
land-use matter is lost is not a bad decision; it is a good-faith negotiation
that ran past a jurisdictional period while everyone was being reasonable.

Every response goes in the file with its date. A refusal with reasons is worth
more to the Kingdom than silence, so ask for reasons and put them in writing if
they are given orally. Where the town moves toward a solution, take it, record
it, and write the letter of thanks; a resolved matter and a working relationship
are worth considerably more than a vindicated one.

---

# 10. Letter to a state legislator

## When to use this

Use it for one of two things: casework, which is a legislative office's
intervention with an agency on a constituent's behalf, or a meeting.

Legislative offices are good at casework and it is under-used. A stalled
application, an agency that will not answer, a licence in limbo, a benefit
wrongly refused — a call from a legislative aide to an agency's liaison moves
files that months of correspondence do not. What legislative offices are not good
at, and will decline, is endorsing an organisation's status, taking a position in
a live dispute between a constituent and a municipality, or intervening in
anything before a court.

The currency here is constituent standing. Members live in the district and vote
in it, and that is the whole basis of the request; it needs no augmentation and no
claim about the Kingdom's status. Nine legislators already know the Kingdom's
name from the Citation of 5 October 2025, which is a real asset with a shelf
life — use it as an introduction, described accurately, never as a claim.

## What must accompany it

For casework: the constituent's written authorisation for the office to inquire
on their behalf — most offices have their own release form, so ask for it first —
and a one-page chronology with file and reference numbers. For a meeting: the
standing statement, and nothing else.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY FIRST-CLASS MAIL

The Honorable [FULL NAME]
[Connecticut State Senate / Connecticut House of Representatives]
Legislative Office Building, Room [NUMBER]
300 Capitol Avenue
Hartford, Connecticut 06106

Re:  [Constituent request — [SUBJECT] / Request for a meeting]
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [Senator / Representative] [SURNAME]:

I write on behalf of Apex Kingdom, a religious society and charitable
trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT]. Our members live, work, and worship
in your district, and [NUMBER] of them are registered voters in
[TOWN].

[WHERE THIS LEGISLATOR IS ONE OF THE NINE WHO INTRODUCED THE
CITATION — CHECK THE FACE OF THE DOCUMENT, AND OMIT THE SENTENCE
OTHERWISE; THE SIGNATURES ARE THE PRESIDENT PRO TEMPORE'S, THE
SPEAKER'S, AND THE SECRETARY OF THE STATE'S, AND TELLING A MEMBER
THEY SIGNED SOMETHING THEY DID NOT IS THE SMALL CHECKABLE ERROR
THIS PACK EXISTS TO PREVENT: You were among the legislators who
introduced the Official Citation the General Assembly issued to the
Kingdom on 5 October 2025, and I am grateful for it.]

[VERSION A — CASEWORK]

I am writing to ask whether your office would make an inquiry on our
behalf with the [AGENCY].

  What is stuck      [ONE SENTENCE — e.g., "An application for
                     [WHAT], filed [DATE], reference [NUMBER]."]
  What we have done  [DATES OF EVERY CONTACT AND ITS RESULT, IN
                     THREE LINES. THE CHRONOLOGY IS ENCLOSED.]
  What we are asking [SOMETHING SMALL AND GRANTABLE — e.g., "that
                     the agency tell us the status of the
                     application and what, if anything, it still
                     needs from us"]
  Who to contact     [NAME], [TELEPHONE], [EMAIL]

We are not asking your office to take a position on the merits, and
we would not want it to. We are asking for the thing a legislative
office can do that we cannot, which is to reach a person who will
answer.

[NAME]'s written authorisation for your office to inquire on
[his/her/their] behalf is enclosed, on your office's form. If you use
a different form, please send it and I will return it the same day.

[VERSION B — A MEETING]

I am writing to ask for thirty minutes with you, or with the
appropriate member of your staff, at your office in Hartford or in
the district, at your convenience.

I would like to introduce the Kingdom's work in [BRIDGEPORT] —
[TWO CONCRETE FACTS: e.g., "a food programme that distributed 4,200
meals last year and a heritage archive open to the public on
Saturdays"] — and to ask your advice about [ONE SPECIFIC THING: e.g.,
"how a small religious charity in the district should approach the
state's heritage grant programmes"].

I am not asking for an endorsement, a resolution, or a statement of
any kind, and I want to say so plainly so that nobody's time is spent
wondering.

[BOTH VERSIONS END HERE]

I will telephone your office on [DATE] to follow up, and I am happy to
work with whichever member of your staff handles this.

Thank you for your service to the district.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Chronology of contacts with [AGENCY]
             2. Constituent authorisation, signed [DATE]
             3. [Statement of institutional standing, for a first
                approach]

cc:          [THE CAUCUS OFFICE STAFF MEMBER WHO HANDLES
             CONSTITUENT MATTERS FOR THIS MEMBER, BY NAME, WHERE
             ESTABLISHED BY TELEPHONE]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Email to the office's published address, with first-class mail behind it, and to
a named staff member wherever one can be identified — casework is done by staff,
and a letter that reaches that person directly is worked the same week.

Be realistic about who that person is. The General Assembly is a part-time
legislature. Most rank-and-file members have neither a district office nor a
personal aide, and staff support runs through the party caucus offices at the
Capitol rather than through the member. Telephone the member's Capitol number,
ask who handles constituent matters for them, and write to that person by name. A
letter addressed to "the district office" of a Connecticut state representative is
addressed to somewhere that does not exist, and a casework request naming nobody
waits for a part-time legislator to open post between sessions.

Timing matters more with a legislature than with any other body in this pack. The
General Assembly sits in a longer session in odd-numbered years and a shorter one
in even-numbered years, and in the closing weeks nothing that is not a bill gets
attention — confirm the current session and adjournment dates before choosing
when to write. Casework in the interim, when members are in their districts, is
answered far faster.

When the office acts, write and say what happened, including when it did not
work. Offices remember constituents who close the loop, and the Kingdom will want
this office again. Record everything in the contact register: which office, which
aide, what was asked, what was done. Aides move, and the file is what survives
them.

---

# 11. Request for a religious accommodation for a member

## When to use this

Use it where a member's religious practice is burdened by an institution the
member is subject to: an employer, a school, a correctional facility, or a
hospital. The Kingdom writes to confirm that the practice is a genuine tenet or
observance of the Kingdom, to describe it precisely, and to ask for a specific
accommodation.

The Kingdom's role is limited and stating the limit is what makes the letter
credible. The Kingdom verifies the religious practice; the member requests the
accommodation. **Do not write this letter without the member's signed
authorisation**, and do not write it at all where the member has not first made
the request themselves through the institution's own process. An organisation
writing over the head of its member, before the member has asked, is an
organisation the institution will treat as the problem.

The law differs by setting and the letter must be adapted, not sent generically.

*Employment.* Title VII requires an employer to reasonably accommodate an
employee's religious observance and practice unless it would cause undue hardship
on the conduct of the business, 42 U.S.C. § 2000e(j). In *Groff v. DeJoy*, 600
U.S. 447 (2023), the Supreme Court clarified that undue hardship means a burden
that is substantial in the overall context of the employer's business, rejecting
the reading of *Trans World Airlines, Inc. v. Hardison*, 432 U.S. 63 (1977),
under which anything more than a de minimis cost sufficed. That is a materially
better standard than employers and their advisers often assume, and saying so
temperately in one sentence is frequently enough. Connecticut's own employment
discrimination statute, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46a-60, prohibits discrimination on
the basis of religious creed and contains a religious-observance accommodation
provision; its subsections have been renumbered in recent years, so confirm the
current designation before citing one. Charge-filing periods before the
Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities and the Equal Employment Opportunity
Commission are short and have changed — confirm both before relying on either,
and note that a missed period is rarely recoverable.

*Correctional.* This engages RLUIPA's institutionalised-persons provision, 42
U.S.C. § 2000cc-1, which prohibits a government from imposing a substantial
burden on the religious exercise of a person residing in or confined to an
institution unless the burden furthers a compelling governmental interest by the
least restrictive means, subject to the jurisdictional conditions that section
states. *Cutter v. Wilkinson*, 544 U.S. 709 (2005), upheld it; *Holt v. Hobbs*,
574 U.S. 352 (2015), applied it and is the case worth knowing, because it turns
on whether the institution actually justified *this* restriction on *this*
person rather than on general deference. Two practical points dominate. The
sincerity of the individual's belief is what matters, not whether the Kingdom is
large or familiar — but a letter from the religious body confirming the practice
removes the commonest ground of refusal. And the incarcerated person must exhaust
the facility's own grievance procedure; 42 U.S.C. § 1997e(a) requires exhaustion
of available administrative remedies before an action is brought, and the
Kingdom's letter supports that process rather than replacing it.

*School.* For a public school the governing framework is the free exercise
clause, the district's own policy, and state law, and the first step is always
the school's written accommodation or excusal procedure. Ask the district for
that procedure rather than citing law at a principal.

*Hospital.* Obligations here arise from the hospital's patient-rights policy,
from the Medicare conditions of participation for a participating hospital, and
from state law; ask which applies rather than asserting one. Note that a hospital
may generally disclose directory information, including to clergy, under the
HIPAA privacy rule at 45 C.F.R. § 164.510(a), subject to the patient's right to
object — but the patient's own written authorisation removes every doubt, and
obtaining it is faster than arguing about the regulation.

## What must accompany it

The member's signed authorisation for the Kingdom to write and to describe their
religious practice. The institution's own form, completed, where one exists. A
short, specific description of the practice. Nothing about the Kingdom's status
beyond one sentence.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY FIRST-CLASS MAIL

[FULL NAME]
[Director of Human Resources / Principal / Warden / Director of
 Chaplaincy Services / Patient Relations]
[INSTITUTION]
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY], [STATE] [ZIP]

Re:  Request for religious accommodation — [MEMBER NAME]
     [Employee / student / inmate / patient number [NUMBER]]
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [SALUTATION]:

I am [FULL NAME], [OFFICE HELD] of Apex Kingdom, a religious society
and charitable trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT]. I write at the request
and with the written authorisation of [MEMBER NAME], who is a member
of the Kingdom in good standing and who has, I understand, made a
request to your [office / facility] dated [DATE]. [His/Her/Their]
authorisation is enclosed.

1. THE RELIGIOUS PRACTICE

   [MEMBER NAME] has been a member of Apex Kingdom since [DATE]. The
   practice in question is [DESCRIBE PRECISELY AND CONCRETELY — e.g.,
   "abstention from work between sunset on [DAY] and sunset on
   [DAY]"; "the wearing of [ARTICLE], which is worn at all times and
   is not removed in the presence of others"; "a dietary observance
   excluding [ITEMS]"; "attendance at a service held on [DAY] at
   [TIME]"]. It is [a tenet / an observance] of the Kingdom, and
   [MEMBER NAME] observes it.

   I confirm the practice as a matter of the Kingdom's religion. I am
   not in a position to speak to anything about [MEMBER NAME]'s
   [employment / studies / custody / care] beyond that, and I do not
   attempt to.

2. THE ACCOMMODATION REQUESTED

   [MEMBER NAME] has asked your [office / facility] to [THE SPECIFIC
   ACCOMMODATION, AS THE MEMBER PUT IT]. The Kingdom supports that
   request and asks that it be granted.

   [WHERE AN ALTERNATIVE WOULD WORK, OFFER IT — THIS IS THE
   PARAGRAPH THAT MOST OFTEN PRODUCES A YES: If the accommodation as
   requested is difficult, [MEMBER NAME] has indicated a willingness
   to [SHIFT SWAP / MAKE UP THE TIME / ACCEPT A DIFFERENT SCHEDULE /
   PROVIDE THE ITEM AT [HIS/HER/THEIR] OWN COST], and the Kingdom is
   willing to [WHAT THE KINGDOM CAN DO — e.g., "provide a member of
   its clergy at no cost to the facility"].]

3. THE FRAMEWORK

   [CHOOSE ONE. DELETE THE OTHERS.]

   [EMPLOYMENT: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 requires an
   employer to reasonably accommodate an employee's religious
   observance and practice unless doing so would impose an undue
   hardship on the conduct of the employer's business, 42 U.S.C.
   § 2000e(j). In Groff v. DeJoy, 600 U.S. 447 (2023), the Supreme
   Court held that undue hardship in this context means a burden
   substantial in the overall context of the employer's business, and
   clarified that the lesser "de minimis" formulation sometimes drawn
   from Trans World Airlines, Inc. v. Hardison, 432 U.S. 63 (1977),
   is not the governing test. Connecticut law separately prohibits
   discrimination on the basis of religious creed and provides for
   accommodation of religious observance, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 46a-60.]

   [CORRECTIONAL: The Religious Land Use and Institutionalized
   Persons Act, 42 U.S.C. § 2000cc-1, provides that a government
   shall not impose a substantial burden on the religious exercise of
   a person residing in or confined to an institution unless the
   burden furthers a compelling governmental interest and is the
   least restrictive means of doing so, subject to the conditions
   that section sets out. I am aware that the facility's security
   judgments are its own, that a court would consider whether this
   particular restriction on this particular person was justified
   (Holt v. Hobbs, 574 U.S. 352 (2015)), and that [MEMBER NAME] must
   pursue the facility's grievance procedure, which [he/she/they]
   [has/have] done under grievance number [NUMBER]. This letter is
   offered to assist that process, not to bypass it.]

   [SCHOOL: I understand the district has a written procedure for
   requests of this kind. If you would send it to me I will make sure
   [MEMBER NAME]'s family completes it correctly. If it has already
   been completed, this letter is offered as the confirmation of
   religious practice that the procedure calls for.]

   [HOSPITAL: I understand this is governed by the hospital's own
   patient rights policy and by its chaplaincy procedures, and I
   would be grateful if you would tell me which applies so that we
   follow it. [MEMBER NAME]'s written authorisation for the hospital
   to communicate with me is enclosed.]

4. WHAT IS ASKED OF YOU

   I would be grateful for a response by [DATE — ALLOW A GENUINE AND
   REASONABLE PERIOD, AND MAKE IT LATER THAN THE INSTITUTION'S OWN
   PROCEDURE REQUIRES WHERE IT HAS ONE]. If it would help to discuss
   this, I am available at the numbers below, and I am content to
   attend in person.

   If the request cannot be granted as made, I would ask that you
   tell [MEMBER NAME] and me what alternative would be workable. In
   the Kingdom's experience these matters are almost always solved by
   a conversation about scheduling, and we would much rather have
   that conversation than anything else.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Authorisation of [MEMBER NAME], signed [DATE]
             2. [The institution's completed form]
             3. [Statement of institutional standing, on a first
                approach]

cc:          [MEMBER NAME]
             [COUNSEL, WHERE THE MATTER HAS ALREADY BEEN REFUSED
             ONCE]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Email and first-class mail, and always a copy to the member. For a correctional
facility, follow the facility's published rules for mail to and about an
incarcerated person exactly; correspondence that does not comply is returned or
simply disappears, and the time lost is time off the grievance clock.

Watch the deadlines that belong to the member rather than to the Kingdom. A
grievance period inside a facility, an employer's internal appeal window, and the
charge-filing periods at the Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities and the
Equal Employment Opportunity Commission all run whether or not this
correspondence is proceeding pleasantly. Tell the member in writing, once, that
those periods are theirs to protect and that they should take independent advice
about them. The Kingdom does not act as the member's lawyer, does not advise them
on their claim, and should say so plainly in its own file.

Record the outcome, whatever it is. A file of granted accommodations, each naming
the Kingdom as the body that verified the practice, is exactly the evidence that
makes the next request easier — and it is a genuine, incremental form of
institutional recognition of the kind `01-LEGAL-POSTURE` § 3(d) describes.

---

# 12. Acknowledgment of an inquiry or of lawful process received

## When to use this

Send it the day anything arrives: an agency inquiry, a subpoena, a summons and
complaint, a notice of violation, an investigative demand, an audit letter, or a
request from a prosecutor.

The rule that governs this entire section can be stated in one line and it is the
most expensive lesson in this library to learn the hard way. **Lawful process is
answered or challenged in court. It is never ignored, and it is never answered
with a document asserting that the issuer lacks authority.** The failure mode is
mechanical: a paper asserting immunity is not read by a court as a legal position,
it is read as non-appearance, and what follows is a default, an order to show
cause, or contempt with sanctions against the officer who signed — on facts that
may have been perfectly defensible had anyone simply appeared. `01-LEGAL-POSTURE`
§ 3(a) sets out the whole mechanism. Appear, then assert. The religious autonomy
doctrines, the ministerial exception, and every privilege the Kingdom holds are
raised in a timely filing by counsel, and they are honoured by the same courts
that would dismiss an immunity claim in a paragraph.

This acknowledgment does not answer the process. It confirms receipt, identifies
counsel, and commits to a date. That is all it does, and it should not be made to
do more.

## What must accompany it

Nothing. And before it goes out, three things happen internally: the document is
scanned and recorded with the date and manner of receipt; counsel is telephoned
the same day; and the litigation hold issues to every custodian per
`05-EVIDENCE-AND-CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY` § 9. Routine deletion after this point is not
routine.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY FIRST-CLASS MAIL

[FULL NAME]
[TITLE]
[BODY]
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY], [STATE] [ZIP]

Re:  [THE MATTER AS THE SENDER STYLED IT, WITH THEIR OWN REFERENCE —
     e.g., "Subpoena duces tecum dated [DATE], [CASE CAPTION], Docket
     No. [NUMBER]" / "Inquiry of [DATE], file [NUMBER]"]
     Acknowledgment of receipt
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [SALUTATION]:

I write on behalf of Apex Kingdom, a religious society and charitable
trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT], to acknowledge receipt of the
[document] above.

  Document received  [DESCRIBE IT AS IT DESCRIBES ITSELF]
  Date received      [DATE]
  Manner of receipt  [BY HAND ON [NAME] AT [ADDRESS] / BY CERTIFIED
                     MAIL / BY EMAIL]
  Compliance or
  response date      [THE DATE STATED IN THE DOCUMENT ITSELF]

The Kingdom takes this seriously and will respond. It has referred the
matter to counsel:

  [FIRM NAME]
  Attention: [ATTORNEY NAME], Esq. (Juris No. [NUMBER])
  [ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

[ATTORNEY NAME] will respond on or before [DATE — THE DATE IN THE
DOCUMENT, OR AN EARLIER ONE, AND NEVER A DATE OF THE KINGDOM'S OWN
INVENTION]. Please direct further communication in this matter to
[him/her/them], with a copy to me.

[WHERE MORE TIME IS GENUINELY NEEDED, ASK — DO NOT ANNOUNCE: The
material sought spans [PERIOD] and is held [DESCRIBE]. Counsel will
contact you within [NUMBER] business days to ask whether you would
agree to an extension to [DATE], or to a narrowing that would let us
produce the most useful material sooner. If an extension is not
agreed, the Kingdom will respond by the date stated in the document.]

[WHERE A PRIVILEGE OR AN OBJECTION IS FORESEEABLE, FLAG IT WITHOUT
ARGUING IT: Some of the material sought may consist of communications
made to clergy in their professional capacity, which Conn. Gen. Stat.
§ 52-146b treats as privileged, or of internal records of religious
governance. Counsel will address any such question with you directly
and, if it cannot be resolved between us, will raise it with the
court in the proper form. The Kingdom is not withholding anything on
that basis today and will not do so without saying so.]

The Kingdom has instructed its officers to preserve all documents and
records that may be relevant to this matter, and that instruction was
given on [DATE].

If any part of this acknowledgment misdescribes what you sent, please
tell me and I will correct my record.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

cc:          [ATTORNEY NAME], Esq., [FIRM]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Email the day of receipt, with first-class mail behind it. Speed is the point:
an acknowledgment on the day, from an organisation that has counsel and a date,
changes how the matter is handled from the beginning.

Some cautions worth stating once, in the order they bite.

Nobody accepts service on behalf of a person who has not authorised it, and no
officer signs anything at the door beyond a delivery receipt. The papers are
taken all the same. Refusing an envelope, returning it unopened, or writing on it
does not defeat service, it is the gesture every account of an organisation of
this kind records, and it costs the Kingdom the only advantage available on the
day, which is knowing what the document says. This
acknowledgment records how the document arrived as a matter of fact and concedes
nothing about whether service was properly made; the manner of service in
Connecticut is governed by Conn. Gen. Stat. § 52-57 and the applicable subsection
turns on the form of the entity served, which is a question for counsel and not
for the person who took the envelope.

The date in the document is the only date that matters, and it is short. A
subpoena in federal civil practice carries an objection period measured from
service under Fed. R. Civ. P. 45(d), with motions to quash or modify governed by
the same rule; state practice differs, and both should be confirmed by counsel
against the current rule rather than assumed. What is never available is letting
the date pass.

Nobody discusses the matter with the issuing body, with the opposing party, or
with anyone outside the Kingdom except through counsel — and internal discussion
happens on channels counsel has approved.

And record the whole of it: the document, the digest, the date and manner of
receipt, the date counsel was instructed, and the date the hold issued. That
sequence, recorded contemporaneously, is what answers the question later put to
every institution in this position, which is what it did in the first
twenty-four hours.

---

# 13. Escalation following no response

## When to use this

Use it after a request has gone unanswered and the follow-up call has been made
and produced nothing. Not before. The value of this letter is entirely in the
dated history it recites, and reciting three dates when two of them were a week
apart makes the Kingdom look impatient rather than diligent.

The letter has one job: to convert "they ignore us" from an impression into a
fact on the record. It does that by listing what was sent, when, to whom, how, and
what came back — nothing else. No grievance, no characterisation, no theory about
why. A schedule of six dated contacts with proof of delivery and three
unanswered is a document that changes behaviour, and it changes it precisely
because it contains no adjectives.

Copying the next authority up is a fact, not a threat, and it should be presented
as one. Choose the right one: for a municipal department, the mayor or town
manager and, where the matter is legal, the town attorney; for a police
department, the chief and then the board of police commissioners where one
exists; for a state agency, the commissioner and then the constituent's
legislator; for records, the Freedom of Information Commission, which is not a cc
but a separate appeal with its own thirty-day jurisdictional window under Conn.
Gen. Stat. § 1-206(b)(1).

## What must accompany it

The schedule of contacts with proof of delivery for each, drawn straight from the
Government-to-Government Contact Register — which is what that register is for.
Copies of the unanswered letters. Nothing new.

## The letter

```
[APEX KINGDOM LETTERHEAD]

[DATE]

BY EMAIL TO [ADDRESS] AND BY CERTIFIED MAIL, RETURN RECEIPT REQUESTED

[FULL NAME]
[TITLE]
[BODY]
[STREET ADDRESS]
[CITY], Connecticut [ZIP]

Re:  [THE MATTER, AS IN THE ORIGINAL LETTER]
     Correspondence of [DATE OF FIRST LETTER] and [DATE], unanswered
     Our reference: [OUR FILE NUMBER — DIGITS ONLY]

Dear [SALUTATION]:

I write on behalf of Apex Kingdom, a religious society and charitable
trust operating in [BRIDGEPORT], further to correspondence with your
office about [THE MATTER], to which we have not yet had a response.

The record of our contacts is as follows.

  [DATE]   Letter to [NAME], [TITLE], requesting [WHAT].
           Sent by [METHOD]; [delivered [DATE], article
           [NUMBER] / read receipt [DATE]]. No response.

  [DATE]   Telephone call to [NAME] at [NUMBER]. [Message
           left with [NAME] / no answer]. No response.

  [DATE]   Second letter to [NAME], referring to the letter of
           [DATE]. Sent by [METHOD]; delivered [DATE], article
           [NUMBER]. No response.

  [DATE]   [ANY ACKNOWLEDGMENT OR PARTIAL RESPONSE, RECORDED
           ACCURATELY — e.g., "Email from [NAME] stating that the
           matter had been forwarded to [OFFICE]. Nothing further
           received."]

I set this out as a matter of record and not as a complaint about any
individual. I appreciate that public offices carry heavy workloads and
that correspondence is sometimes mislaid, which is why I have
attached copies of everything above.

What was asked, and is still asked, is this: [RESTATE THE ORIGINAL
REQUEST IN ONE SENTENCE, UNCHANGED. DO NOT ENLARGE IT. AN ESCALATION
THAT ALSO EXPANDS THE ASK INVITES THE ANSWER THAT THE MATTER IS NOW
TOO COMPLICATED TO DEAL WITH QUICKLY.]

[WHERE THERE IS AN AUTHORITY OBLIGING A RESPONSE, CITE IT ONCE AND
WITHOUT MENACE — e.g., "The request of [DATE] was made under the
Freedom of Information Act, Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-200 et seq. Section
1-206(a) provides that a failure to comply within four business days
is deemed a denial, and I note that the period has passed." — WHERE
THERE IS NO SUCH AUTHORITY, SAY NOTHING AND DO NOT INVENT ONE.]

I would be grateful for a response by [DATE, AT LEAST TWO WEEKS OUT].
If it would be easier to deal with this by telephone or in person, I
am available at your convenience and will come to your offices.

If this matter is not your office's to answer, please tell me whose it
is and I will write to them directly; I would rather be redirected
than persist with the wrong office.

If I have not heard by the date above, the Kingdom will [STATE WHAT IT
WILL ACTUALLY DO, AND ONLY WHAT IT WILL ACTUALLY DO — e.g., "write to
the Office of the Mayor"; "file a notice of appeal with the Freedom of
Information Commission under Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-206(b)(1)"; "ask
its counsel to advise it"]. I would much prefer not to, and I am
writing now precisely so that it is not necessary.

Respectfully,

______________________________
[FULL NAME]
[OFFICE HELD], Apex Kingdom
[STREET ADDRESS] · [TELEPHONE] · [EMAIL]

Enclosures:  1. Letter of [DATE], with proof of delivery
             2. Letter of [DATE], with proof of delivery
             3. [ANY ACKNOWLEDGMENT RECEIVED]

cc:          [THE NEXT AUTHORITY UP, BY NAME AND TITLE — e.g., "The
             Honorable [NAME], Mayor of the City of [BRIDGEPORT]"]
             [COUNSEL, WHERE ENGAGED]
```

## Delivery, and what to do with the answer

Certified mail with return receipt and email, both recorded. This is the one
letter in the pack where certified mail is unambiguously right, because its
subject is the reliability of delivery.

Then do the thing stated. A follow-up date that passes without the stated step
teaches the office, correctly, that the Kingdom's dates mean nothing, and no
later letter recovers from that. Conversely, an escalation that does exactly what
it said it would, no more and no less, establishes something about the Kingdom
that is worth more than the request at issue.

Escalate one level at a time. A first unanswered letter that is copied to the
mayor, the city attorney, and a state senator does not produce three times the
pressure; it produces an office that treats the Kingdom as a problem and hands
the file to counsel. And keep the tone flat throughout, because this letter has a
second reader. If any of this is ever litigated or heard by a commission, the
escalation letter is the exhibit — and the version with no adjectives in it is
the one that makes the point.

---

# What never goes out over the Kingdom's name

Every letter in this pack works because of what is absent from it. The list below
is not a matter of taste or of tone, and none of it is negotiable by an officer
having a bad week. Each item converts an institution with real grievances into a
defendant, and the mechanism is given for each because officers who understand
the mechanism do not drift.

**Anything styled as process.** A summons, subpoena, warrant, writ, citation to
appear, lien, levy, distraint, seizure order, notice of default framed as a
judgment, "affidavit of truth", or UCC-style filing — anything wearing the dress
of a court order, whatever it is called. Filing a false lien or encumbrance is
criminal in Connecticut, and filing one against a federal officer or employee on
account of their official duties is a felony under 18 U.S.C. § 1521 carrying up
to ten years. The forgery provisions at Conn. Gen. Stat. § 53a-137 et seq. reach
the rest. The moment such a document exists, the Kingdom is a criminal defendant
rather than a complainant, its leadership is personally exposed, its charitable
status is in jeopardy, and every official who would have taken a meeting has a
file explaining why they should not.

**Any assertion of sovereignty, immunity, or want of jurisdiction.** A private
association has no sovereign immunity — it belongs to the federal government, the
states, foreign states under the Foreign Sovereign Immunities Act, and federally
recognised Indian tribes, and it is not something an entity confers on itself in
its own founding document. Asserted to an agency, the claim is wrong and the
recipient's law department knows it is wrong, and the letter is routed to the
population of correspondence that is never answered on the merits. Asserted to a
court instead of appearing, it produces a default judgment. Everything the
assertion was meant to protect — church autonomy under *Watson v. Jones*,
*Serbian Eastern Orthodox Diocese v. Milivojevich*, and *Jones v. Wolf*, the
ministerial exception under *Hosanna-Tabor* and *Our Lady of Guadalupe School*,
RLUIPA, RFRA, and arbitration on consent under 9 U.S.C. § 2 — is available, is
honoured, and is forfeited by asserting the thing that is not.

**Anything resembling a law-enforcement credential.** A badge, shield, patch,
uniform, warrant card, identification card, vehicle marking, or plate suggesting
a governmental body or peace-officer authority. Holding a private officer out as
a peace officer is criminal impersonation under Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 53a-130 and
53a-130a; federally, 18 U.S.C. § 701 reaches unauthorised official insignia,
§ 912 false personation of a federal officer, and § 1028 fraudulent
identification documents. One incident ends the municipal relationship
permanently and personally, and it ends it for everyone in the organisation
rather than for the individual who did it. This is why event volunteers are
stewards in plain vests and why the Kingdom offers no marshals to any police
department, ever.

**Diplomatic framing addressed to a domestic authority.** "Note verbale",
"ministry of foreign affairs", "consular", "diplomatic immunity", "ambassador to
the United States", "government-to-government" said to a town hall. These are the
recognised markers of sovereign-citizen filings. The consequence is not that the
recipient disagrees; it is that the correspondence is flagged rather than read,
and in a police context it can convert a complainant into a subject — which is the
precise opposite of what letters 4, 6, and 8 exist to achieve. The abbreviation
counts as much as the phrase. The contact register numbers its records
`AK-G2G-000000`, and those three characters are that phrase in a form a reader
decodes in about a second, which is why the reference printed on an outgoing
letter is the digits and nothing else.

**Instructions to anyone to refuse lawful process,** to decline to identify
themselves to a police officer, or to assert that a court lacks jurisdiction over
them. Beyond what it does to the person who follows the instruction, it is the
single fact most likely to characterise the Kingdom in any account written about
it afterwards.

**The Citation oversold.** The Official Citation of 5 October 2025 is genuine,
sealed, introduced by nine legislators and signed by the President Pro Tempore,
the Speaker, and the Secretary of the State, and it is worth being proud of. It
is a ceremonial honour recognising contribution to cultural heritage, civic
education, and community empowerment. It confers no legal status, is not state
recognition of a tribe, and creates no government-to-government relationship.
Every official the Kingdom writes to knows this, because their office issues
them. Described accurately it opens doors. Presented as recognition of status it
tells the reader that the sender either misunderstands the instrument or will
misdescribe one, and that judgment attaches to everything else in the envelope.

**A claim of a corporate form the Kingdom does not hold,** a determination letter
it has not received, insurance it does not carry, or a membership figure it
cannot support from its own rolls. Each of these is small, each is checkable, and
a municipal attorney who finds one keeps it. The credibility this pack is built
on comes from the fact that everything in it can be verified — which is also why
the standing statement gives the register's public verification address and
invites the recipient to use it.

---

*This is an operating template pack prepared to organise the Kingdom's affairs and
to keep its officers on defensible ground with public bodies. It is not legal
advice and no attorney-client relationship arises from it. Statutes are amended
and renumbered, forms of address and office holders change, agency and
departmental procedures differ from one town to the next, and several of the
matters touched here carry filing and appeal periods that cannot be reopened once
missed. Confirm every citation and every interval against the current General
Statutes, the current rules, and the body's own published procedure before
sending, and engage licensed Connecticut counsel before acting on any of it.*
